newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary police say synagogue not target of bomb.
newsitem.headline: Hungary police say synagogue not target of bomb.

text.p: A bomb exploded in the Hungarian capital on Wednesday but police said it was probably not aimed at a nearby synagogue and eyewitnesses said it was more likely that a massage parlour was the target.
The bomb, the 12th in two months, had been left in a dustbin near Europe's largest synagogue, the Dohanyi Utca, and hurled debris up to 100 metres (yards) but caused no injuries.
A homemade bomb, also placed in a dustbin, exploded near the Synagogue in October, causing no injuries.
"It was too far from the synagogue to make a link," national police spokesman Andras Rozsa told Reuters, adding that there were no injuries.
Eyewitnesses said a more likely target was a first-floor massage parlour in the building closest to the blast.
"It was right in front of the parlour," said a local resident, Tamas Szigeti. "I'm sure that's what they were looking for."
Since September, Budapest residents have been rattled by 12 bombings and five shootings, apparently part of a war among criminal gangs. One man has been fatally shot and two have been badly injured.
The blasts mostly targeted businesses, nightclubs and sex bars and seemed aimed at intimidating the owners, police said.
Wednesday's explosion was heard several blocks away in the centre of the city's commercial district.
"It was such a big bang I thought the windows would break," said Ilona Parizs, 57, a retired teacher who lives nearby.
The Hungarian government sacked the chiefs of the national and Budapest police on Friday for failing to halt what seems like a gangland war.
